critique: The black field and hot pale-yellow/orange flash color are appropriate, and the flash clearly advances to the right between 0.01 and 0.08. However, it is still a very small, soft, horizontally oval cloud rather than the large explosive directional muzzle-flash form. The leading edge is not a sharp flame wedge, there is no substantial fading trail behind the ignition point, and no separated fast sparks are visible. The motion reads as a compact particle clump translating rightward instead of an expanding forward blast.

suggestions.why: Reduce the burst from thousands of overlapping cloudlets to a shorter, more legible ignition event so directional structure can become visible instead of a solid round blob.
Keep the fast right-moving main particles alive long enough to form a clearly tapering flame/trail behind the leading flash.
Smaller main particles reduce the inflated pill-shaped silhouette and reveal a sharper, more explosive directional edge.
Increase auxiliary emission so the blast gains visible detached ember/spark detail rather than reading as one uniform cloud.
Allow auxiliary sparks to persist into the late frame, creating a readable trailing energetic scatter behind the forward flame.
